corrections.source_says: Specify the scoring procedure for both outcomes: a condition-blind student assistant classified ideas using the Specht and Buck category system, which has 13 categories within five clusters. Seven uncategorized ideas and all deleted ideas were excluded. Each participant's score is the number of distinct categories covered; S1-O1 includes accepted/copied AI suggestions, while S1-O2 excludes AI-origin ideas. These are within-participant flexibility scores, not diversity across different people.

The scored lists were produced during the brainstorming session with AI suggestions available in that arm. Excluding AI-origin ideas from S1-O2 is an analysis of human contributions made during that same session, not an outcome collected after AI removal; question=with_ai is correct.

confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion and all 10 PDF pages, including references; no appendix is included. source.version correctly identifies the published HICSS-57 proceedings paper (2024), by Lucas Memmert and Eva Bittner; PDF p. 1 (printed p. 421), heading and byline, and pp. 9-10 (printed pp. 429-430), end matter.

The study is a reanalysis of a randomized, between-person AI-assistance experiment conducted during university courses. field_rct and context_class=none are supported; this belongs in the two-screener pipeline, not the AI-versus-human context class. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 424), Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), Section 4.

The study reports 54 participants before two exclusions, leaving 52 analyzed students, 26 per arm; it is not an experiment with fewer than 50 analyzed people. The total and arm counts at randomization are not separately identified, so the existing null n_randomized values are appropriate. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), Section 4, opening paragraph.
The participant quote matches: age mean=22.3, min=18, max=37; gender 8 female and 44 male; students enrolled mostly in informatics programs. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), Section 4, opening paragraph.

People brainstormed food-waste solutions for 10 minutes, with approximately 30 minutes for the entire study. The AI arm could request suggestions and copy them into its idea list; only accepted suggestions counted toward its final output. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 424), Section 3.1.

The tool was gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 at temperature 0.9, returning 3 suggestions at a time through the study app, using the current human and previous AI ideas in its prompt. PDF p. 4 (printed p. 424), Section 3.2 and Figure 2; PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), Section 3.2 continuation.

Both existing outcomes correctly use flexibility, with_ai, category_count, and participant: they count distinct categories within each participant's idea list. They do not measure similarity across different participants or creativity after AI removal. PDF pp. 5-6 (printed pp. 425-426), Sections 3.3 and 4.1.

S1-O1.reported and the corresponding one-line finding match the PDF exactly: human+AI mdn=5 versus human-only mdn=2; U=546.5, p<.001; rank-biserial correlation rB=.617. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 426), Section 4.1, first paragraph and Figure 3.

S1-O2.reported and the corresponding one-line finding match the PDF: excluding AI-origin ideas, U=326.0, p=.830, with no significant condition difference. The accompanying text does not give arm-specific medians, means, SDs, or an effect size for that comparison. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 426), Section 4.1, paragraph accompanying Figure 4.

The count of 600 is ideas, not people: Table 2 gives 373 AI-origin and 227 human-origin ideas. The primary final-list flexibility analysis includes 115 accepted/copied AI suggestions, not all 373 AI suggestions. PDF p. 5 (printed p. 425), Table 2 and Section 4.1 continuing on PDF p. 6 (printed p. 426).

The paper is not a synthesis and reports no pooled meta-analytic estimate; the default synthesis fields are appropriate. Its origin-based exploratory comparisons do not constitute a separate independent randomized study. PDF pp. 4-7 (printed pp. 424-427), Sections 3-4.3.

No company involvement is disclosed. The named research funder is the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research; using an OpenAI model alone does not establish company participation in the research. PDF p. 9 (printed p. 429), Acknowledgment, and PDF p. 4 (printed p. 424), Section 3.2.
summary: The paper contains a randomized AI-assistance study with 52 analyzed students, and the reported flexibility results match the PDF. Corrections are needed for core eligibility, exclusions, sample overlap, incomplete outcome fields, and omitted fluency outcomes.
